newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Bargain hunting sends Seoul shares to higher close.
newsitem.headline: Bargain hunting sends Seoul shares to higher close.

text.p: Bargain hunting, active buying in financial shares and easing pressure from margin loan calls sent shares higher across the board on Thursday, brokers said.
The composite stock index provisionally ended 18.46 points, or 2.97 percent, higher at 639.87.
Advancers outpaced decliners, 696 to 132, while an active 35.99 million shares changed hands.

Bargain hunting emerged after the market touched the psychologically significant support line of 600. "The 600 bottom seems confirmed for the time being, so investors are buying with more confidence," said a Ssangyong Securities broker.
"Buying in banks, especially, dragged the index higher today," he added. Brokers said there were still lingering hopes that the government would soon step in to boost the market.
On Wednesday, finance ministry officials said the government was considering boosting measures.
Banks and other financial stocks have risen on expectation of active mergers and acquisitions this year.
SEOULBANK shares led the market, rising 350 won to 4,770. Korea First Bank was 270 won higher at 5,000.
Bargain hunting was active in small and mid-sized shares that had sharply fallen in recent days after pressure to pay back margin loans eased, brokers said.
Loans for margin trading as of Monday stood at 2.76 trillion won, while customer deposits at brokerages were valued at 2.29 trillion won.
Ssangyong Motor shares fell 600 won to 9,700 on profit taking after climbing to a high of 10,900.
The shares rose on recurring rumours, denied by the company, that it was the target of a takeover bid by the Samsung group.
The index futures March contracts ended 0.20 of a point higher at 65.50 while the KOSPI-200 index gained 2.06 points to end at 68.42.
